chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about fasting three days in the month, is there a making up for it upon the traveler? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: Does a traveler need to make up missed optional fasts?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the distinction is drawn between obligatory fasts, which require makeup, and voluntary (nafl) fasts, which do not. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential principle that the concessions (rukhas) granted to travelers in the Quran apply specifically to mandatory acts of worship, thereby relieving the believer of the burden of making up missed voluntary days. It underscores the flexibility and ease (yusr) inherent in Shia fiqh regarding supererogatory acts.
